result.description: Intuit QuickBooks Online: cloud accounting software; developer platform exposes Accounting and Payments APIs for third-party apps.
result.auth_detail: OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow against Intuit's authorization server for the Accounting REST API itself (the 'com.intuit.quickbooks.accounting' scope; bearer access token ~60 min, refresh token). Intuit's own oauth-jsclient/SDKs implement it for API calls, and the MCP server merely reuses the same OAuth2 app credentials. No per-user API keys.
result.access_detail: Free Intuit developer account gives app creation, development keys and sandbox companies. Production keys for use with other users' live companies require filling Intuit's app questionnaire/assessment (and a compliance review for listing on the App Store). Docs pages were JS-rendered, so this is not verbatim-confirmed.
result.api_notes: QBO Accounting REST API with CRUD on ~29 entity types (customers, invoices, bills, payments, etc.), query endpoint, batch, 11+ reports; separate Payments API and other Intuit APIs. Intuit's MCP server wraps 145 tools over it.
result.blocker: Production use against other users' live companies needs Intuit app review/assessment; refresh tokens rotate; redirect URIs must be https in production.

evidence.quote: If you only want to read your own company's data, you still need to set up an app — Intuit does not offer per-user API keys.
